weekly_marks.summary:
## Week 1 summary for the operator

Closed the week at **−$38.72 (−0.39%)** — a scratch, which beats a red week given the macro setup. The single losing trade (NVDA scout, −$38.72, −4.63%) was the entire drawdown; the stop was honored same-session without hesitation, which is the discipline rep I want to keep. The win of the week was *not trading* through the FOMC + MSFT/META/GOOGL + AAPL/AMZN binary stack — sitting in cash with no info edge was the highest-EV move. Re-engaged Friday with a small GOOGL post-earnings starter (2sh @ $385.69, 7.75% book) which closed flat. Book enters next week 92% cash + GOOGL, with a live floor exception through NFP (5/8) and a hard commitment to deploy toward the 15% floor by Mon 5/11. Key playbook upgrades: minimum 1.5× ATR distance from entry to invalidation (the NVDA stop was inside the day's range — statistically dead), no piggyback trades on someone else's binary, and the next conditional entry must be staged *before* exiting the current one.

## Week 2 summary for the operator

Closed the week at **+$54.96 (+0.55%)** week-on-week, lifetime **+$16.24 (+0.16%)** — first green close and capital intact. The trade that booked the week was the GOOGL add @ $388.43 on 5/5 (bull flag, gap retest hold), which lifted the position to full-size 16% deployment, cleared the TREND-UP floor by mechanism rather than exception, and is now +3.55% unrealized into the weekend. The discipline rep of the week was the RM rejection of the GOOGL +2sh @ $399 add on 5/6 — would have breached the 20% single-name rail and concentrated 24% pre-NFP/Powell. The pattern to fix: deployment math was wrong twice (used entry cost / starting cash, not MV / PV), triggering two unnecessary floor exceptions; the AMZN $268 limit was left stale as price drifted to $275+. Playbook upgrades for next week: recompute deployment from the live snapshot every tick; refresh-or-cancel any limit >2 sessions old; write floor commitments as state-dependent conditionals, not calendar IOUs. Entering 5/11 with $8,413 cash, GOOGL 4sh, stale AMZN limit to address Monday open, and CPI Tue/Wed + Powell 5/15 as the dated risks to plan around.

## Week 3 summary for the operator

Closed the week at **−$16.08 (−0.16%)**, lifetime back to roughly flat at **+$0.16**. Zero trades executed — the entire weekly P&L was mark-to-market on the single GOOGL position as it gave back ~1 point into the Friday risk-off tape (PPI hot, SPY −1.2%, Powell-succession headlines). The wins of the week were process wins: cancelled the stale AMZN $268 limit on Monday open (clean execution of wk2 lesson #2), kept deployment math correct from the live snapshot every tick (no needless floor-exception cycles), and refused to chase a "diversification" scout into Friday's binary handoff. The pattern to fix: the 5/8 conditional ("if NFP cooperative + GOOGL holds $392 Monday → MSFT/AMZN scout") was met on 5/11 and silently deferred into CPI, then into Powell, then into the weekend — an open-ended "maybe" instead of a real trigger, which left the book as 100% GOOGL beta all week. Playbook upgrades: conditionals must execute when conditions are met (adjacent binaries adjust *size*, not whether to act); when the book holds N=1 position, diversification trumps scaling; hard backstops are immutable until the +5% trail trigger fires (caught a $15 upward drift on the GOOGL hard stop). Entering 5/18 with $8,413 cash, GOOGL 4sh @ +2.51%, and a clean Mon/Tue window for an MSFT or TSM scout before NVDA earnings (5/27) becomes the next binary.

## Week 4 summary for the operator

Closed the week at **−$48.92 (−0.49%)**, lifetime back into the red at **−$48.76 (−0.49%)** — capital largely intact but a step back from last week's scratch. Five trades: MSFT scout (5/18, still open at −1.17%), GOOGL stop-out 4sh (5/19, +$2.40 realized), GOOGL re-entry 2sh (5/20, $388.91), GOOGL stop-out 2sh (5/21, −$2.50 realized). The win of the week was finally executing the wk3-deferred MSFT diversification on Monday — direct lesson-uptake, conf properly dialed for the rates headwind. The loss of the week was the 5/20 GOOGL re-entry at $388.91, *below* the pre-committed $393 reclaim trigger, justified as "floor diversification" but actually a revenge trade into a still-broken setup that stopped out 24 hours later. The 5/22 phantom-GOOGL incident (trader proposed selling a position we no longer held) exposed a process gap: the static "current book state" block in the playbook rotted within 24h of Monday's trades and was operated against. Playbook upgrades: re-entry triggers are binding contracts (not soft suggestions), stop discipline always overrides the floor, every tick reconciles from the live snapshot rather than the markdown header, and a dialed-down confidence should also dial down *entry timing* (limit at technical level, not market into close). Entering 5/26 (Tuesday, post-Memorial-Day) with $9,114 cash, MSFT 2sh under water, an active floor exception expiring at Tue close, and NVDA earnings Wed AMC as the week's main binary — diversification window is essentially Tuesday morning only.
